A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnthroTAP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices. Inspection of all 17 pages in each version supports reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original tracker-training experiments, TAP-Vid and RoboTAP results, dataset analyses, and component ablations in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original training and evaluation results and adds Anthro-TAPNext experiments and pseudo-label accuracy measurements against human annotations.

M1.justification: The TokenHMR/SMPL projection, ray-casting visibility, optical-flow filtering, and use of trackers' original losses remain unchanged. TAPNext receives the existing pseudo-label supervision; no new algorithmic adaptation is documented. Expanded filtering explanations match the existing Appendix C equations.

E1.justification: The represented datasets, domains, and point-tracking task remain unchanged. The new human-annotation check evaluates trajectories within the already-used Let's Dance domain, while TAPNext uses existing DAVIS and RoboTAP benchmarks. These additions change evaluation procedures and results rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TAPNext and BootsTAPNext alongside Anthro-TAPNext, retaining the previous comparator set. The new pseudo-label validation also compares against LocoTrack predictions. This is a focused extension of the comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds TAPNext evaluation at 256 × 256 and a manual-reference validation protocol on Let's Dance using 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16-pixel accuracy thresholds. The former complexity/diversity subset and no-visibility controls disappear. Existing benchmark modes, LocoTrack training settings, and retained ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the downstream complexity/diversity training analysis in v2 Table 6 with direct pseudo-label validation against human annotations. It also removes the visibility-prediction ablation from v2 Appendix A, Table 11, without relocation. This substantially changes the diagnostic evidence, although filtering, clip-length, dilation, and data-scale ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for performance. The unchanged standard-deviation-based trajectory diversity metric is a dataset descriptor, not performance uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 1 results include Anthro-TAPNext's DAVIS Strided AJ of 71.4 versus BootsTAPNext's 68.9 at 256 × 256; its RoboTAP AJ is lower, 63.4 versus 64.1. New Table 6 reports average positional accuracy of 64.5 for AnthroTAP pseudo-labels versus 56.1 for LocoTrack. The earlier complexity/diversity and visibility ablation results disappear. Retained result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the explicit ray parameterization and intersection inequalities with an equivalent geometric visibility rule. Appendix C's filtering equations and Appendix D's complexity/diversity definitions, equations (1)–(15), remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly includes proposed trajectory complexity/diversity metrics in the contribution statement and removes full-open-sourcing language. The central claims of scalable human-motion supervision, data efficiency, and state-of-the-art general-domain tracking remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a mechanism explanation involving optical flow following an occluder or becoming inconsistent with body motion. The BlinkVision discussion more explicitly attributes the advantage to real-world appearance over annotation precision, and the new annotation study is interpreted as validating supervision quality. Appendix F's substantive limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 describes filtering explicitly as occurring before training and adds a supplementary hyperparameter pointer. It removes the abstract's explicit code/data-release promise, while retaining the project URL and open-sourcing discussion. Existing numerical training and hardware details remain; no actual resource-availability change, additional threshold values, or TAPNext-specific training recipe is established.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to TAPNext and TAPIP3D and removes the separate DAVIS 2016 reference while retaining DAVIS 2017. TAPNext also enters the empirical positioning. The broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged; L4P's bibliographic revision refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Targeted edits tighten the ray-casting explanation, expand filtering prose, standardize self-training terminology, remove duplicated BlinkVision discussion, and relocate the trajectory-metric overview. v3 also adds an equal-contribution footnote, acknowledgments, and a supplementary-material heading. The overall section structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised and relabeled, Table 1 gains a TAPNext block, Table 6 is replaced, and Table 11 is removed. Several captions and table highlights change; Figure 6 moves from page 12 to page 11. The remaining qualitative figures and overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds valuable cross-model evidence in Table 1 and direct pseudo-label validation in Table 6. However, it removes experiments linking trajectory complexity/diversity and visibility prediction to downstream gains. The new annotation study lacks sample counts and annotation procedures, and TAPNext-specific training details are absent. These limitations make it unclear whether the added validation outweighs the lost diagnostic support.
